description: We are keen to learn more about space and explore what else is out there
summary:
Left Behind, Still Talking is an interactive, story-driven web experience built for school-age space enthusiasts (ages 8–14) to explore the historic NASA hardware left on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space since the 1960s.

Organizing 55 years of space exploration into three cosmic neighbourhoods—the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space—the platform shows young learners which spacecraft are still working, which completed their missions, and which have gone silent. Users can watch an animated 1972–2026 trajectory route map of Voyager 1, Voyager 2, Pioneer 10, Pioneer 11, and New Horizons; track a live countdown to Voyager 1 reaching one full light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026; filter 13 iconic missions by operational status; flip interactive science cards; test their knowledge in a 6-question quiz; and use a customizable Hallway Scale Builder to pace out solar system distances in meters.

By turning complex orbital distances, light-speed communication delays, and decades of mission history into hands-on visual tools, Left Behind, Still Talking helps students and classrooms connect with the robotic pioneers that continue to expand human knowledge.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Left Behind, Still Talking introduces school-age space fans (ages 8–14), teachers, and science clubs to the NASA spacecraft, rovers, helicopters, and instruments left across the solar system. It breaks 55 years of exploration into three accessible neighbourhoods—The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space—highlighting each piece of hardware's name, launch/landing year, current status (Still Working, Mission Ended, or Gone Silent), and the scientific discoveries it enabled.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Live Light-Day Countdown & Animated Starfield: Opens with a live countdown timer to November 18, 2026, when Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object to reach one full light-day (~25.9 billion km / 173 AU) from Earth.

2. Three Cosmic Neighbourhoods:

- The Moon: Features an animated Earth-to-Moon laser diagram illustrating how Apollo 11's unpowered retroreflectors measure the Moon's ~3.8 cm/year drift (~2.17 m since 1969).

- Mars: Showcases Sojourner, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Ingenuity, including a visual comparison bar contrasting Opportunity's planned 90-day mission against its actual ~14-year lifespan.

- Deep Space & The Golden Record: Features a spinning illustration of Voyager's Golden Record and prompts students to imagine what sound from their own town they would send to the stars.

3. Interactive 1972–2026 Deep Space Route Map: An animated SVG trajectory map lets users play, pause, or scrub a timeline slider from 1972 to 2026 to watch Voyager 1, Voyager 2, Pioneer 10, Pioneer 11, and New Horizons travel past the outer planets and heliopause, updating a live table of AU/km distances and one-way radio travel times.

4. Filterable Fleet Directory & Scrollable 55-Year Timeline: Lets learners filter 13 spacecraft by status ("All", "Still working", "Mission ended", "Gone silent") and scroll through key milestones from 1969 to 2026.

5. Interactive Science Flip-Cards, Hallway Scale Builder & Space Quiz:

- Hardware Became Answers: Four tap-to-flip cards explaining how moonquakes, Martian lakebeds, Io's volcanoes, and the heliopause were discovered.

- Build the Solar System in a Hallway: Lets students input a custom scale for 1 Astronomical Unit (e.g., 1 AU = 1 meter) to calculate exact hallway distances to Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Voyager 2, and Voyager 1.

- Quick Space Quiz: A 6-question interactive quiz with instant scientific feedback and mission rank scoring.

BENEFITS & ACCESSIBILITY

Built as a single, zero-dependency HTML file (`index.html`), the project runs offline or online in any browser, supports automatic light and dark color schemes, includes full ARIA accessibility labels, and respects `prefers-reduced-motion` settings for inclusive classroom use.

TOOLS & CODING LANGUAGES USED

- Languages: Semantic HTML5, modern CSS3 (Grid, Flexbox, custom properties, keyframe animations), and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).

- Graphics & APIs: Custom inline SVG diagrams, HTML5 2D Canvas starfield particle engine, and IntersectionObserver API for scroll-triggered animations.

- Typography: Google Fonts (Space Grotesk) with automatic system sans-serif fallback for offline use.
